articleBody:
Before bringing in a contractor to frame your garage, checking key structural and functional details will ensure your project runs smoothly and stays on budget.

- [ ] Concrete slab inspection — Ensure the concrete floor is level, cured, and free of severe cracks that could shift your bottom plates.
- [ ] Moisture barrier check — Confirm that pressure-treated bottom plates are specified wherever lumber meets the concrete slab directly.
- [ ] Wall layout markings — Chalk out wall lines, including rough openings for planned doors or windows, to verify clear vehicle clearance.
- [ ] Heavy storage mapping — Note exactly where heavy utility shelving, workbenches, or tool cabinets will hang so solid backing studs get installed.
- [ ] Electrical and utility plans — Mark planned locations for subpanels, 240V outlets, and lighting so framing studs leave ample room without crowding boxes.
- [ ] Fire separation verification — Check whether your garage shares a common wall or ceiling with living spaces that requires specific stud spacing.
- [ ] Insulation depth planning — Confirm that stud depth (such as 2x4 versus 2x6) matches the insulation R-value you plan to install later.
- [ ] Building permit verification — Verify whether your city or county requires framing permits and inspections before any wall coverings go up.

How to use this checklist:
Walk through your garage with this list and a tape measure before requesting framing bids. Identifying where cabinets, storage racks, and wiring boxes will sit saves you costly alterations after the lumber is nailed into place.
